# Collaboration protocol

How Pavol and Claude work together on the Fortress revival. This is the
operating manual for Claude sessions in this repository: read it at session
start, before doing anything else. It was reconstructed from session
transcripts after repeated context compactions eroded it; committing it here
is the fix.

Provenance marks: **(P)** = Pavol's words, in-session or in the handover
document; **(i)** = inferred from a repeated correction, not stated
verbatim. Rules marked (i) are real — they were each learned the hard way —
but if one seems to conflict with something Pavol says, his words win.

## 1. Roles

- **(P)** Claude explains the codebase and produces documentation and
  experiments as we go; **Pavol decides what gets committed.**
- **(P)** When in doubt, ask before acting. Surface discrepancies and diffs
  to Pavol; do not resolve them silently.
- **(P)** Standing approval exists for exactly two things: *"I approve the
  above modernization plan. Continue autonomously. Delegate to workers where
  it makes sense."* — scoped to the approved ladder in
  `modernization-plan.md`, not a general license — and the `main`
  fast-forward standing order in §4.
- **(P)** Use idle time — "there's no need for you to idle with empty
  hands." While waiting on builds or feedback, advance parked research or
  documentation.
- **(P)** But don't freestyle new deliverables before discussion — goals
  are discussed first, then the work is produced.

## 2. Tone and custodianship

- **(P)** "No self congratulatory tone. We are humble custodians here. We
  deserve no credit." This applies to READMEs, commit messages, docs,
  everything committed.
- **(P)** Attribution to the original authors is mandatory, reconstructed by
  hand where git history can't carry it (see `research/authorship.md`).
- **(P)** No unactionable comments in the source tree; provenance commentary
  belongs in commit messages.
- **(P)** Epistemic humility: verify against primary sources before
  asserting. Claims in old READMEs describe their eras, not the current
  tree.

## 3. Presenting work

- **(P)** Documents for approval are presented as rendered artifacts, not
  diffs: draft in the scratchpad, publish via Artifact, give Pavol the URL.
- **(P)** Feedback arrives in batches, often from mobile. Default mode:
  hold edits, acknowledge briefly, process the batch when told. Pavol marks
  actionable exceptions explicitly ("...now").
- **(P)** Terse mode when requested.
- **(P)** Offer numbered options and help decide; pushback is welcome.
- **(i)** Never use the AskUserQuestion dialog — it has broken repeatedly.
  Present options as plain chat text.
- **(P)** Ask clarifying questions when goals are unclear; **(i)** flag
  interpretation risks rather than silently assuming.
- **(P)** Teach, don't gloss. Detailed explanatory reports are first-class
  deliverables, not overhead.

## 4. Commit and push discipline

- Work branch: `claude/handover-reading-vn8zgr`. Never push to a different
  branch without explicit permission (the `transcripts` orphan branch and
  the `main` fast-forward below are the two standing exceptions; a third,
  2026-09-18 **(P)**: agents of a Workflow batch commit and push to their own
  `wip/<slug>` branch as they work, so a dead container loses nothing —
  "perfectly reasonable. I'm giving you my explicit yes").
- **(P)** Standing order — fast-forward `main` after every working-branch
  push: `git push origin claude/handover-reading-vn8zgr:main`. Established
  2026-08-19 ("If green, fast-forward main and proceed to JDK 11") for
  gated rungs, practiced and ratified for doc/plan/spec commits too —
  2026-08-23: "fast forward main as has been our standing practice."
  Act-then-report; do **not** re-ask (the re-ask after a compaction is what
  prompted this entry). Whenever `origin/main` is behind the working-branch
  tip, ff it. This continues through the clean-ladder migration: Pavol
  renames branches via the GitHub UI himself when it's done.
- Commit-and-push-as-you-go for approved work; gated changes stay
  uncommitted until the gate is green.
- No pull requests unless explicitly requested.
- Never commit: HANDOVER.md or ZIP contents without Pavol's explicit
  go-ahead; copyrighted PDFs and decks (`research/decks/` is gitignored —
  reference by Wayback URL, never commit the PDF); model identifiers in any
  committed artifact.
- `research/extracts/` holds only our own summaries with brief attributed
  quotations, never document reproductions.
- Generated-source churn is a regression to investigate, not noise to
  revert.
- **(i)** 2026-09-19, after 85 MB of a worker's experimental caches reached
  `main`: a worker's evidence enters the tree by an explicit list of files,
  never by copying a directory; and a staged change of more than a few
  hundred lines is looked at (`git diff --cached --stat`) before it is
  committed. `.gitignore` covers the tree's own cache location, not cache
  files placed anywhere else.
- Commit footer, exactly:

  ```
  Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
  Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01LjDz79rDLErtnSKpovMDpX
  ```

- Pavol's email is for identification and attribution only; never send it
  to any service.
- **(i)** Edits under the original Fortress tree (the historical artifact)
  are flagged explicitly at commit time.
- **(i)** Don't invent standing orders: a rule cited as Pavol's must trace
  to his words; own inferences are flagged as such (hence the provenance
  marks in this file).
- **(i)** The stop hook is advisory: decline its commit demands while held
  or gated changes exist. **(P)** 2026-09-19: decline them silently — "I don't
  really need to hear about those reminders at all"; never mention a hook
  reminder to Pavol.

## 5. Delegation and context hygiene

- Delegate by default. The main session does high-level coordination; bulk
  reads, transcript recovery, and big searches go to worker agents.
  Compacting instead of delegating is a failure mode Pavol has called out.
- **(P)** 2026-09-19, restated after the coordinator traced the STM's
  provenance and the numeric tower by hand: repository exploration — finding
  where a mechanism lives, tracing where code came from, surveying files —
  goes to a worker that returns a summary; the coordinator's reasoning is
  kept for high-level work. And after a compaction `coordinator/FACTS.md`
  is read whole, in one pass, never the tail alone.
- **(P)** 2026-09-19, when the coordinator had queued the repair batch's process
  review behind the running climb: work with no dependency on what is running is
  delegated at once, not queued — "I see no dependency — why can't subagent(s)
  investigate these now?"
- **(P)** 2026-09-19, after the coordinator listed the harness's task
  directory and the scratchpad at boot to find out whether two workers had
  finished, and put some 150 file names into its own context — "you listed
  its working directory and flooded your context with that": which workers
  are in flight is read from the harness's own notice at the top of the turn
  and from the one output path the handover names, tested with `test -f`;
  no directory under the scratchpad or the task directory is listed at boot;
  every boot command bounds its output (`head`, `wc -l`, `--stat`), and a
  command whose output could exceed a screen is given to a worker, not run by
  the coordinator.
- **(P)** 2026-09-20: workers run on the best tier Pavol can afford, Opus today,
  never lower; a Fable worker only when he has said yes to that piece. (The
  2026-09-18 "by the alias" remark meant only that the script need not change when

Author: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

    widen, narrow, unsigned and signed on the compiler prelude's four fixed-size integers
    
    The four conversions are declared on trait ZZ32, ZZ64, NN32 and NN64 over the
    getters and natives the prelude already had. widen sign-extends from ZZ32 and
    zero-extends from NN32; unsigned and signed reinterpret the bits; narrow throws
    IntegerOverflow when the value does not fit, on both the signed and the
    unsigned side. That last is a decision, not a reading: no prose chapter names
    narrow, and the argument is the prelude's own convention that a plainly-named

    tests/UnsignedTest.fss:210-211, which assert the interpreter's truncating
    answers, unpassable on the compiled path, and that consequence is ledger row
    346 rather than hidden. NN64.coerce(x: NN32) sign-extended and no longer does.

Line numbers in `Library/FortressLibrary.fss` and `.fsi` below are those of this rung's branch
after its own edit. If rung L is applied first, as the gather's ordering rule makes it (its lowest

## FACTS.md

- **The four comments of 2026-09-21 are in the interpreter's library, and they change nothing the interpreter or the checker computes** (2026-09-22, rung C of climb batch 3, `compile-ladder/rung-library-comments/REPORT.md`). The tower closure carries the team's own `NOT YET` note for the clause the grammar cannot write, `comprises Integral[\I\] where [\I\]` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:613` under `trait AnyIntegral`, `.fsi:410` in the `.fsi`'s `not yet:` form); `Array3`'s `excludes AnyAdditiveGroup` says which of two rank-3 futures it takes (`.fss:2671-2676`, `.fsi:1661-1666`): a user operator between an `Array3` and a lower-rank array, pinned on a cold cache by `ProjectFortress/tests/ArrayOperatorsBesideLibrary.fss:23-24`, against a rank-3 additive group; the (number, `Array3`) case is the scalar block's own; the scalar block says its eight return the unsized `Array[\T,I\]` (`.fss:4504-4508`, `.fsi:2547-2552`) and that the reversed `-` is `y - e` elementwise, the block's one order-dependent pair (`.fss:4512-4514`, `.fsi:2556-2558`). Comment text only, 31 inserted lines: `compile-ladder/rung-library-comments/comment-only-check.py` re-lexes both files with `Spacing.rats`'s rules (0 deleted, 0 non-comment lines added, token streams identical); the gate's checker-count stage reads 93 errors at 52 locations before and after, and its whole output is identical line for line once positions are mapped back (`probes/post-edit-comparisons.txt`); `walk` on a probe of all four declarations prints the same 17 lines, and the gated `ArrayOperatorsBesideLibrary` loads and passes on a cold cache of the branch's library (`probes/gated-cold-postrepair.txt`). Finished prose, ready to paste. Nothing here was written into the coordinator's files. Line numbers are today's, on the base `d610695c0`. Every cited line also names its symbol, for re-anchoring. Rungs L and C edit `Library/FortressLibrary.fss` and `.fsi`, and one of their edits touches a line cited here: rung L edits `FortressLibrary.fsi:373` in place (`comprises { ... }` → `comprises { AnyIntegral }`, `explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-3.md:97`). The line does not move, so the citation of `trait QQ` at `:373` survives. Every other edit of L and C in those two files is below the lines cited here (`CLIMB-BATCH-3.md:94`, `:96`, `:107-110`). Rung S adds an import line at `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fss:282` (`CLIMB-BATCH-3.md:134`). If it adds one line, the new row's `CompilerBuiltin.fss:927` (`trait RR64`'s `coerce(x: FloatLiteral)`) and `:991` (`trait FloatLiteral excludes {RR32, RR64}`) each move down by one, and the symbols named beside them re-anchor them.

## FACTS.md

One bullet, under "The compile-path ladder baseline", after the last rung entry:

- **`round` on a float sends an exact half to the even integer on both paths as of rung R of climb batch 3** (2026-09-22, `compile-ladder/rung-round-half-even/REPORT.md`). The interpreter's two float natives, `Float$Round` and `RR32$Round`, are now `(long) Math.rint(…)` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/glue/prim/Float.java:384`, `RR32.java:326`), the call the compiled path's `simpleDoubleArith.doubleRound` has made since rung F (`nativeHelpers/simpleDoubleArith.java:132-134`). A float literal reaches `Float$Round` through `trait Number`'s `round` body (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:422`), so those two natives are every float `round` in `walk`. `walk` now answers `round(2.5) = 2`, `round(-3.5) = -4`, `round(0.5) = 0` and `round(-1.5) = -2` on `RR64`, and the same plus `round(4.5) = 4` on `RR32`, gated by `ProjectFortress/tests/RoundHalfEvenRungR.fss` (21 assertions). Its compiled twin prints the same eleven `RR64` lines as `walk` (`compile-ladder/rung-round-half-even/probes/RoundHalfEvenCompiledProbe.txt` against `compile-ladder/rung-round-half-even/probes/RoundHalfEvenWalkProbe-after.txt`). Nothing changed at the edges on either path. NaN still gives 0. +∞ and values at or past 2^63 saturate to 2^63−1, and −∞ and values at or below −2^63 to −2^63. A numeral within half an ulp of a tie is still rounded as its nearest double on both paths, where the specification makes it a rational: `round(2.50000000000000001)` is 2, and the specification says 3. That defect is recorded in a new ledger row (provisional number 354, below) and gated as an expected failure by `ProjectFortress/tests/XXXRoundNearTieNumeral.fss`. `testSystem` has 386 tests: `RoundHalfEvenRungR.fss` is in shard 3 and `XXXRoundNearTieNumeral.fss` in shard 1.

## Ledger note

Append to the notes of **row 329**:

> **Fixed \<short hash\> (rung R of climb batch 3, 2026-09-22, `compile-ladder/rung-round-half-even/REPORT.md`).** `Math.round(x)` → `(long) Math.rint(x)` in `Float$Round` (`Float.java:384`), and the same token in `RR32$Round` (`RR32.java:326`). `RR32$Round` is the second float native of the same 2008 commit `e67394471`, and this row's text did not name it. Gated by `ProjectFortress/tests/RoundHalfEvenRungR.fss` (RR64 literal and `Float` operands, and RR32).
> - It is red before the edit (`compile-ladder/rung-round-half-even/probes/failure-before-edit.txt`: `a Long: 3 =/= a Int: 2`).
> - It is green after (`compile-ladder/rung-round-half-even/probes/pass-after-edit.txt`, and `OK (1 test)` under `SystemJUTest` in `compile-ladder/rung-round-half-even/probes/harness-after-edit.txt`).
> - `walk` and the compiled path now print the same eleven `RR64` values, ties and edges (`compile-ladder/rung-round-half-even/probes/RoundHalfEvenWalkProbe-after.txt` against `compile-ladder/rung-round-half-even/probes/RoundHalfEvenCompiledProbe.txt`).
>
> This row's four ties (2.5, −3.5, 0.5 and −1.5) are exactly representable. So when they are written as numerals, half to even on the nearest double is the specification's answer (`literals.tex:162-163` with `numbers.tex:470-472`). As `Float` values, which is how this row's probes build them (with `SQRT`), the prose is silent and the decision of 2026-09-21 stands in for it. A numeral whose rational value is not its nearest double, such as `2.50000000000000001`, belongs to the provisional row opened beside this one.
>
> Some line numbers in this row have moved:
> - the rational body (`trait QQ`'s `round`) is at `Library/FortressLibrary.fss:592`, not `:589`;
> - `trait Number`'s `round` is at `:422`, not `:419`;
> - `trait QQ` is at `Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:373`, not `:370`;
> - the compiled pin (`round 2.5 = 2`) is at `ProjectFortress/library_tests/RR64FunctionsRungF.fss:87-90`, not `:98-101`.

## Provisional new row (numbered by the coordinator; 354 is the next free on d610695c0)

This number is provisional. Other rungs of this batch may propose rows too, and the gather assigns the final numbers in manifest order (P, L, C, R, S, M). The row is written in the ledger's column shape (`explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md:113-114`), ready to paste:

| 354 | **a numeral with a radix point is rounded, floored, ceiled and truncated as its nearest double, not as the rational it denotes, on both paths**. In `walk`, the library declares the numeral a floating-point value: `object FloatLiteral extends RR64` (`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss:194`), and `trait RR64 extends Number comprises { Float, FloatLiteral, RR32, QQ }` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:425`, `.fsi:338`). `object FloatLiteral` declares no `round`, `floor`, `ceiling` or `truncate` (`FortressBuiltin.fss:195-200`), so they are `trait Number`'s bodies over `asFloat(self)` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:417`, `:419`, `:421`, `:422`). `FloatLiteral$AsFloat` is `Double.valueOf` of the numeral's digits (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/evaluator/values/FFloatLiteral.java:39-40`), although `FFloatLiteral` keeps a radix-ten numeral's digits exactly (`:17`, `:28`). The interpreter has no coercion mechanism (`coordinator/map/spec-to-implementation.md:288`). On the compiled path, the prelude has no ℚ: `QQ` occurs zero times in `CompilerBuiltin.fsi`, `CompilerBuiltin.fss`, `CompilerLibrary.fsi` and `CompilerLibrary.fss`. The prelude declares `trait FloatLiteral excludes {RR32, RR64}` (`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fss:991`), and `trait RR64`'s `coerce(x: FloatLiteral) = x.asRR64` (`:927`) turns the numeral into a double before `RR64.round`. Measured, identical on both paths after rung R: `round(2.50000000000000001)` = 2 (spec 3), `round(0.50000000000000001)` = 0 (spec 1), `round(3.49999999999999999)` = 4 (spec 3), `floor(2.99999999999999999)` = 3.0 (spec 2), `ceiling(2.00000000000000001)` = 2.0 (spec 3) and `truncate(2.99999999999999999)` = 3 (spec 2). | NEGATIVE-VERIFIED | library gap vs spec | `basic/expressions/literals.tex:132` (numerals are not directly converted to any number type), `:146-148` (library coercions take compound numerals to rationals), `:162-163` ("Numerals containing a radix point are actually rational literals"); `basic/lexical-structure.tex:1137-1138` (a numeral with a `.` is compound); `basic-lib/numbers.tex:461` (`round(self): ℤ` on ℚ), `:464-472` (`floor`, `ceiling`, and `round` half to even, of "this rational number") and `:474-477` (`truncate`). `literals.tex:170-173` (one rounding when a rational static expression is part of a floating-point computation) does not reach it: the only `round` the prose defines for a rational is ℚ's, and no float operand is present | `compile-ladder/rung-round-half-even/probes/skeptic/SkNearTie.fss` + `.txt` (both paths; the rational body's answers at `.txt:21-24`, from `SkNearTieRational.fss`), `compile-ladder/rung-round-half-even/probes/skeptic/SkNearIntNumeral.fss` + `.txt` (both paths) | ours (climb batch 3, rung R, first skeptic) | Gated by `ProjectFortress/tests/XXXRoundNearTieNumeral.fss` (four `round` numerals, the specification's answers) as an expected failure. It was shown red on a deliberate local fix, a temporary `FloatLiteral$Round` over `BigDecimal` `HALF_EVEN` of the digits, and an expected failure again after the fix was reverted (`compile-ladder/rung-round-half-even/probes/xxx-numeral-red-on-deliberate-fix.txt`, `compile-ladder/rung-round-half-even/probes/xxx-numeral-after-revert.txt`). `floor`, `ceiling` and `truncate` are carried here without an `XXX` file of their own: they have one cause and one repair with `round`, and a file that asserted them too would stay red through a `round`-only repair. Before rung R, `walk`'s half-up gave the specification's `round` on two of the four numerals by coincidence (`2.50000000000000001` → 3, `0.50000000000000001` → 1), because their nearest doubles are exact ties that half-up sends upward. Rung R moved those two to 2 and 0, and `2.49999999999999999` from 3 to 2. No rule applied to the double can answer all of them: `2.50000000000000001`, `2.49999999999999999` and `2.5` share the double `2.5` and want 3, 2 and 2. The same cause shows in comparison and arithmetic: under `walk`, `2.50000000000000001 = 2.5` is `true` and their difference is `0.0`, while the numeral prints its own digits (`compile-ladder/rung-round-half-even/probes/NumeralAsDoubleProbe.txt`). **The fix is a fork, and the decision is Pavol's.** (a) The narrow patch: `object FloatLiteral` gets the four methods over the exact decimal (`BigDecimal` of the digits `FFloatLiteral` keeps, with `HALF_EVEN`, `FLOOR`, `CEILING` and `DOWN`), in `walk` now and on the compiled side with the one library at the switch-over. It is about 30 lines. The numeral then rounds as a rational but compares and subtracts as a double, an inconsistency inside one value, and the return types interact with row 330. (b) The design: a compound numeral becomes a rational value, as the prose says. Either `FloatLiteral` leaves `RR64` for ℚ, or the one library gets the specification's coercion once the checker's coercion machinery runs on the library route. The cost: every float expression that mentions a literal goes through exact rational arithmetic and one conversion (`literals.tex:170-173` allows exactly that); the hot float paths of rows 302 and 303; `List[\FloatLiteral\]` inference (row 20); `FFloatLiteral.seqv`; ℚ is absent from the compiler prelude until the one library; and the checker's numeral typing (row 325) is the static half. (c) The team's design stands: a compound numeral is an `RR64` value, recorded in `POSITIONS.md` as a decision against the prose. The `XXX` file is then deleted and the row closes as design. The gate is right under (a) and (b), and is removed under (c). Relations: row 325 is the integer half of the same absence, since the numeral types of `literals.tex:83-131` exist nowhere in the implementation; row 330 decides the return types these methods will have. |

The count stage's `#total` is **93** before this rung (`compile-ladder/rung-analyzer-memo/probes/checker-count-preedit.txt`, byte-identical to `compile-ladder/gate-baseline/checker-count.txt`) and **93** after it on its own branch (`probes/checker-count-postedit.txt`); the two tables are identical line for line, `#locations 52`, the `nat` crash line and `#shadow` fresh included. ## The FACTS.md line

- **The checker's clause memo: `TypeAnalyzer.parents` and `excludesClause` are memoized per trait table, and nothing the checker answers changes** (2026-09-22, rung M of climb batch 3, `compile-ladder/rung-analyzer-memo/`). The two functions re-instantiated a trait's `extends` and `excludes` clauses with a whole-type substitution on every call, `excludesClause` recursing over every supertrait — 87% of the checker's JFR samples had `substitute` on the stack and 86% were under these two functions' lambdas (`perf-probes/nat/followup/f3-jfr-top.txt:40-44`). They read nothing but the trait table and the type (`scala_src/types/TypeAnalyzer.scala:722-727`, `:747-762`; `TypeAnalyzerUtil.substitute` is pure, `:35-60`), so the memo lives on `TraitTable` (`scala_src/typechecker/TraitTable.scala:81-97`), which every analyzer `extend` makes from one check shares, behind the switch `fortress.analyzer.clauses.cache` (default on; `FORTRESS_ANALYZER_CLAUSES_CACHE=false` turns it off). `TypeAnalyzer.scala` changes at the two `def` lines only and gains no line. The table has no mutator and every "new" table is a new object with empty memos (eight construction sites); the checker is single-threaded (all JFR samples on `main`), and the maps are `ConcurrentHashMap`s anyway, filled by `get`/`putIfAbsent` because `excludesClause` recurses into its own map. Measured on the stock tree, switch on against off: the checker-count stage 9.5-12.4 s against 22.3-22.6 s (three alternating runs each, `probes/timing.txt`), the compiler prelude's library-order build 129 s against 196 s (one run each); and no answer changed — six count tables and their full checker output identical to the stock run's, the prelude's 462 class files (556 files with the 94 `.xlation` files) byte-identical and every file its build left in `analyzed_cache/` identical (the on-side listing was not captured before the corpus pass overwrote it, `probes/differential.txt:38`; the skeptic's rebuild enumerates 15 for the prelude, 12 `.tfi`/`.tfs` at the top of `analyzed_cache/` and 3 under `depends/`, `probes/skeptic/prelude.txt:25-41`; every file present was compared and identical on both runs), all 435 `compiler_tests` units' compile outputs identical, and the 2,049 class files and 230 analyzed-cache files they left byte-identical (`probes/differential.txt`), the six analyzer JUnit classes green both ways. The batch record's "21 s → 13 s in the tree's own terms" compared the `nat` shadow with the memo against the stock tree; the stock tree with the memo alone is the measurement above. Not measured: the suites (the gate's), the per-declaration run of `followup.md:70` on the stock tree.

## The ledger note

**Open a row, provisionally numbered 354** (provisional: another rung of this batch may open one too, and the gather assigns the final numbers in manifest order P, L, C, R, S, M). It belongs in section 10, "Bytecode-compiler path", because the static checker runs only on that path. ##### summary

The closure the compiled path needs is that sentence or a sub-rule of it, and the sentence is triage decision (b), reserved to Pavol by the batch record (CLIMB-BATCH-3.md:18; triage.md:113).

##### forPavol
THE FORK. The compiled checker's checkP is the 2011-2012 team's "multiple instantiation exclusion" (Papers/Types/exclusion.tick:141-152; justificationOfRTR.tex:496-497). The specification refuses it (types-vals-vars.tex:184-189; trait-parameters.tex:359-367 and :383-397, whose object Empty belongs to every instantiation of List) and the library route needs it gone (61 of the 93 errors, CLIMB-BATCH-3.md:73). Removing it in any placement opens one hole: the compiled overloading checker's Return Type Rule trusts the single instantiation the rule used to guarantee (OverloadingOracle.scala:88-95), and a six-line program then type-checks and dies with IncompatibleClassChangeError (probes/ProbeMIEPick.fss; probe-matrix.txt:67, :89, :111). Which rule replaces that reliance is yours, because the natural one is the sentence already reserved to you as triage decision (b).

CANDIDATES AND COSTS. (a) The specification's sentence, overloading.tex:100-108: overloads of a name share their static parameters, one instantiation per call site. Closes the hole; the checker's side of the instantiation question goes away. Cost: refuses generic-beside-non-generic sets that have no hole — compiler_tests/Compiled12.invariantInference.fss:52-61 (gated by its .test), Compiled6.ak.fss:14-15, Library/Generator2.fss:52-57, four interpreter tests (overloadTest8, doubledOverloading, GeneratorNullPointer, ArrayListQuick/PureListQuick) — so gated tests would be rewritten, itself a reserved stop (PLAN.md:52); the triage's 35 library sites, already errors, then need renames not a checker accommodation; and "static parameters" for functional methods of generic traits must be defined (triage.md:57-59) or the sentence refuses overrides. (b) The hole's exact shape as a sub-rule of the sentence: refuse a pair where one declaration has static parameters the other lacks and the generic one's return type depends on such a parameter, unless the more specific return type is a subtype with the parameter held rigid. Closes the hole, refuses nothing the specification permits, accepts every corpus site above, leaves decision (b) untouched; one edit in OverloadingOracle.satisfiesReturnTypeRule. Cost: sound only if the code generator dispatches generic overloads at the call site's instantiation — unmeasured; a probe (generic-beside-generic with different bounds, on a multiply-instantiated object, static type one instantiation) settles it, and if dispatch is by inspection the rule must widen to generic-beside-generic pairs, which is then against the specification in that corner. (c) The interpreter's rule (OverloadedFunction.java:496-498), under which the library was written: against the specification for same-parameter generic overloads with unrelated overlapping domains; compiled cost unmeasured. (d) Keep the rule: against the specification and the library route; not r

RECOMMENDATION. (b), landed in one rung together with the relaxation (hierarchy questions plus the overloading check, as the record placed it), preceded by the codegen measurement; the full sentence stays your separate decision (b) on the library evidence and subsumes it if taken. That rung also lands ProbeMIEPick as a gated compile-error test, converts XXXExclusionRelaxRungP to the positive test, and records that the overloading half refuses Tag[\ZZ32\] beside Tag[\String\] (probe-overload.txt:12-19) as the specification's Meet Rule taking effect, not a regression.
